title: Tutorial: Repeat a Resource With count
scenario: count creates several instances of one resource block. Each instance gets an index, which you can use to pick the matching value from a list. Create one bucket per entry in a list.
constraints: Set count from the length of var.bucket_names.

focus.title: Repeat the bucket
focus.todo: Add the repetition count and select a name for each instance.

hints.why: count is the smallest step from one resource to many. It also reveals why Terraform addresses instances by index, which is useful when you later compare count with for_each.
hints.what: Complete the bucket resource body. It needs one argument that creates one instance per list entry and one argument that picks the matching name for the current instance.
hints.when: Use count when the instances are interchangeable and the list order is stable. If each instance has a durable name, for_each is safer.
hints.how: Find the resource block and add the two arguments that depend on the list. One makes the number of instances, the other reads the current position. The output already shows how to collect every instance.

test_manifest.title: bucket_names is declared as a list
the resource uses count or for_each
